questions.question: Article 74 of the Constitution elaborates on which of the following?

options.text: Appointment of Chief Justice by President
Appointment of Vice President by President
Council of Ministers to aid and advise President
Appointment of Chairman of Finance Commission

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Council of Ministers to aid and advise President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 74 of the Indian Constitution mandates that there shall be a **Council of Ministers, headed by the Prime Minister, to aid and advise the President** in the exercise of their functions.
 
• The President is bound by the advice provided by the Council of Ministers **except in cases where discretion is explicitly permitted by the Constitution**.
 
• The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, as per Article 75(3) of the Constitution.
 
• This provision ensures that the President functions as a constitutional head, with real executive power vested in the Council of Ministers.
 
• The advice provided by the Council is confidential, and the President cannot question it publicly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prime Minister:** The leader of the Council of Ministers and is appointed by the President. The PM is the principal channel of communication between the President and the Council.
 
• **Collective Responsibility:** The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, ensuring that they act as a united entity in governance.
 
• **Discretionary Powers of the President:** The President can use their discretion in certain situations, such as appointing the Prime Minister in case of a hung parliament.
 
• **Executive Powers:** While the President is the nominal executive, the real executive authority rests with the Council of Ministers led by the Prime Minister.
 
• **Article 75:** This article further elaborates on the appointment and tenure of the Council of Ministers, including the provision that they hold office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.question: How many medals did India win in the ISSF World Championship 2023 event?

__
 
• India won a total of **14 medals** at the ISSF World Championship 2023.
 
• The medal tally included **6 gold medals**, **6 silver medals**, and **2 bronze medals**.
 
• India's stellar performance secured the country the **second position** on the medal table, behind China.
 
• Rudrankksh Patil and Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar were among the standout performers, winning individual gold medals in their respective shooting events.
 
• This achievement highlights India's growing prominence in the sport of **shooting** at the international level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ISSF (International Shooting Sport Federation):**

 
 
• The ISSF is the governing body for the sport of shooting worldwide, conducting world championships and other international competitions.
 
• The federation was founded in 1907 and is headquartered in Munich, Germany.
 
• It oversees events across various shooting disciplines, including rifle, pistol, and shotgun.
 
 
 
• **India's Shooting Success:**
 
 
• India has been emerging as a powerhouse in shooting sports, with significant investments in athlete training and infrastructure.
 
• The consistent performances at international events have contributed to India's strong position in the global rankings.
 
 
 
• **Notable Indian Shooters:**
 
 
• Rudrankksh Patil, Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar, and Divyansh Singh Panwar have been some of the prominent names in recent shooting events.
 
• These athletes have consistently delivered podium finishes in major international competitions.

• The support of initiatives like the Khelo India program has been instrumental in nurturing young talent in the sport.

questions.question: Government of India Act of 1935 had ___________ schedules.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India Act of 1935 contained **10 schedules**, which provided detailed information about administrative divisions and governance.
 
• The schedules outlined provisions related to **federal structure, provincial autonomy, and other administrative details**.
 
• The Act served as the basis for the **constitutional framework of British India**, influencing future constitutional developments.
 
• The 10 schedules included subjects like **allocation of powers, franchise qualifications, and provisions for minorities**.
 
• Though implemented partially, it was the **largest and most detailed act** passed by the British Parliament for India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Federal Structure:** The Act proposed an all-India Federation, including British provinces and princely states, though the federation was never realized.
 
• **Provincial Autonomy:** Significant autonomy was granted to provinces, allowing them to legislate on subjects listed in the Provincial List.
 
• **Diarchy Abolished:** Diarchy, introduced under the Government of India Act, 1919, was abolished at the provincial level, giving ministers more authority.
 
• **Inspiration for Indian Constitution:** The Act's provisions on federalism, administrative divisions, and governance influenced the drafting of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Schedules in Indian Constitution:** The concept of schedules was carried forward into the Indian Constitution, which currently has **12 schedules**.

questions.question: Which type of industry deals with the reproduction and multiplication of plants and animals for sale?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Genetic Industry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Genetic industry** focuses on the reproduction, multiplication, and breeding of plants and animals for commercial purposes.
 
• This industry involves activities such as **animal husbandry, fish farming, forestry, and plant nurseries**.
 
• Products from genetic industries are used for consumption, agriculture, or further industrial processing.
 
• It is considered a part of primary industries as it deals with naturally occurring resources and their improvement.
 
• Examples include **breeding high-yield crops, aquaculture, and livestock farming**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Extractive Industry:** Deals with extracting natural resources such as minerals, oil, and gas from the earth.
 
• **Manufacturing Industry:** Involves converting raw materials into finished goods, such as in factories producing cars or electronics.
 
• **Service Industry:** Provides intangible services to customers, such as healthcare, education, or hospitality.
 
• **Genetic Resources:** Include germplasm, seeds, and genetic material used in plant and animal breeding for enhanced productivity.
 
• **Importance of Genetic Industry:** Helps improve agricultural yield, ensure food security, and support sustainable practices through advancements in biotechnology and breeding techniques.

questions.question: In which year was the Bengal Partition of 1905 reversed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1911**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bengal Partition of 1905, implemented by Lord Curzon, divided Bengal into East Bengal and West Bengal based on religious demographics.
 
• It was reversed in **1911** due to widespread protests, boycotts, and the Swadeshi Movement led by Indian nationalists.
 
• The reversal coincided with the shifting of the capital of British India from Calcutta (now Kolkata) to Delhi in the same year.
 
• The annulment was seen as a victory for Indian nationalism but led to further communal tensions in the region.
 
• After 1911, Bengal was reunited as a single province under British India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Partition of Bengal (1905):**

 
 
• Implemented by Lord Curzon, the Viceroy of India, to improve administration efficiency.
 
• It divided Bengal into East Bengal (Muslim-majority) and West Bengal (Hindu-majority).
 
• The move was criticized as a deliberate attempt to divide Hindus and Muslims.
 
 
 
• **Swadeshi Movement:**
 
 
• Launched as a protest against the partition, promoting the boycott of British goods and the use of Indian-made products.
 
• Key leaders included Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Lala Lajpat Rai.
 
• It played a significant role in the rise of Indian nationalism.
 
 
 
• **Delhi as Capital:**
 
 
• In 1911, the British shifted the capital from Calcutta to Delhi to strengthen their imperial control.
 
• Delhi was considered geographically strategic for administrative purposes.
 
• The coronation of King George V in Delhi marked this significant change.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Reversal:**
 
 
• While the reversal of Bengal's partition was celebrated, it sowed seeds of communal tensions between Hindus and Muslims.
 
• It eventually contributed to the broader demand for separate electorates and later, the creation of Pakistan in 1947.

questions.question: Organisms, when faced with new circumstances and surroundings, start adapting new characters to fit into their environment. This is termed as _____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Behavioural Adaptation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Behavioural adaptation** refers to changes in an organism's behaviour that enhance its ability to survive and reproduce in a specific environment.
 
• These adaptations may include activities like migration, hibernation, or changes in feeding habits to cope with environmental challenges.
 
• For example, birds migrating to warmer climates during winter is a common behavioural adaptation.
 
• Organisms often develop behavioural adaptations in response to changes in food availability, predation pressure, or climatic conditions.
 
• Such adaptations help organisms maintain homeostasis and increase their chances of survival in changing environments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adaptation:** A process by which organisms adjust to new environmental conditions over generations, ensuring survival and reproduction.
 
• **Types of Adaptations:** There are three main types—structural (physical features), physiological (internal body processes), and behavioural (actions or responses).
 
• **Hibernation:** A behavioural adaptation where animals enter a dormant state to conserve energy during extreme environmental conditions, such as winter.
 
• **Migration:** Seasonal movement of organisms from one habitat to another, often driven by the need for food, mating, or suitable climatic conditions.
 
• **Mimicry:** A form of adaptation where organisms imitate the appearance or behaviour of other species to avoid predation or attract prey.

questions.question: How does a budget deficit affect a nation's economy?

options.text: It indicates a surplus in government spending.
It may lead to increased government borrowing.
It results in a decrease in public spending.
It always leads to immediate economic growth.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It may lead to increased government borrowing.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A budget deficit occurs when a nation's expenditures exceed its revenue, resulting in a shortfall that needs to be financed.
 
• Governments often address budget deficits by borrowing funds, typically through the issuance of bonds or other debt instruments.
 
• Increased borrowing can lead to a rise in national debt, impacting economic stability and future fiscal policies.
 
• Excessive government borrowing may increase interest rates, as higher demand for capital competes with private sector borrowing.
 
• Persistent budget deficits can lead to inflationary pressures if financed through monetary expansion, reducing the purchasing power of money.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Debt:** The accumulated borrowing of a government over time, inclusive of interest payments, often measured as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
 
• **Fiscal Policy:** Government strategies for managing revenue and expenditure to influence the economy, including measures to control deficits.
 
• **Inflation:** A sustained increase in the general price level of goods and services, often exacerbated by deficit financing through excessive money supply.
 
• **Bond Issuance:** A common method for governments to borrow money, where investors lend funds in exchange for periodic interest payments and repayment at maturity.
 
• **Crowding Out Effect:** When increased government borrowing limits the availability of funds for private sector investment, potentially slowing economic growth.

questions.question: Identify the classical dance form that is the principal dance of Northern India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kathak** is one of the eight classical dance forms of India and is primarily associated with **North India**.
 
• The name "Kathak" is derived from the Sanskrit word "**Katha**," which means "story," as the dance form is based on storytelling through expressive movements and gestures.
 
• Kathak has three major gharanas (schools): **Lucknow, Jaipur,** and **Banaras**, each known for its unique style and emphasis on different elements of the dance.
 
• This dance form is characterized by intricate **footwork** (tatkar), graceful movements, and **spins** (chakkars), complemented by facial expressions and hand gestures.
 
• Kathak has a strong connection with both **Hindu mythology** and **Mughal court traditions**, showcasing a blend of devotional and secular themes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Classical Dance Forms of India:** There are eight recognized classical dance forms in India: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Odissi, and Sattriya.
 
• **Gharanas:** The Lucknow gharana emphasizes **grace** and **expressive storytelling**; the Jaipur gharana focuses on **intricate footwork**; and the Banaras gharana is known for its **spiritual themes**.
 
• **Instruments in Kathak:** Common accompanying instruments include the **tabla**, **pakhawaj**, **sitar**, and **sarangi**, which provide rhythm and melody to the performance.
 
• **Costumes:** Traditional Kathak costumes for women include **Anarkali suits** with dupattas, while men wear **kurta-churidar**. Both often feature intricate embroidery and embellishments.
 
• **Bol (Syllables):** Kathak dancers use rhythmic syllables called "**bols**" to synchronize their movements with the music, creating a captivating performance.

questions.question: Which of the following Union Ministries introduced The Bills of Lading Bill, 2024 in August 2024 in the Lok Sabha?

options.text: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bills of Lading Bill, 2024, was introduced by the **Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways** in August 2024 in the Lok Sabha.
 
• The bill aims to replace the existing legislative framework governing **bills of lading**, which are key documents in maritime trade.
 
• It seeks to modernize and streamline the process of issuing and managing bills of lading in line with **international best practices**.
 
• This legislative update is expected to **enhance transparency, reduce fraud, and improve efficiency** in India’s shipping and trade sector.
 
• The bill is part of India’s broader efforts to strengthen its **maritime and logistics infrastructure** to support its growing economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bill of Lading:**

 
 
• A bill of lading is a legal document issued by a carrier to acknowledge receipt of cargo for shipment.
 
• It serves as a shipment receipt, a document of title, and a contract between the shipper and the carrier.
 
• Digitalization of bills of lading is a growing trend globally to improve efficiency in maritime trade.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways:**
 
 
• This ministry is responsible for formulating and implementing policies related to shipping, ports, and waterways in India.
 
• It oversees major ports, inland waterways, and maritime trade regulations.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the development of India’s maritime infrastructure to boost economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Maritime Trade in India:**
 
 
• India has a coastline of over 7,500 km and relies heavily on maritime trade for its economic activities.
 
• Approximately 95% of India’s trade by volume and 70% by value is conducted through maritime routes.
 
• Modernizing laws and infrastructure is essential to support India’s role in global trade.
 
 
 
• **International Maritime Organization (IMO):**
 
 
• The IMO is a specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for regulating shipping.
 
• It promotes safe, secure, and efficient shipping on clean oceans.
 
• India’s new bill aligns with IMO standards to improve global interoperability in maritime trade.

questions.question: ‘Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar’ of the Sangeet Natak Akademi is NOT awarded in which of the following categories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Literature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar' is awarded by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi**, an autonomous body under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India.
 
• The award recognizes outstanding achievement by young artists in the fields of **Music, Dance, and Theatre**.
 
• This puraskar specifically aims at promoting young talent in performing arts and is intended for artists below the age of 40.
 
• **Literature** is not included as a category for the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar, as it focuses solely on performing arts.
 
• The award was instituted in **2006** to honor the legacy of Ustad Bismillah Khan, the legendary shehnai maestro.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi:** It is India’s national academy for performing arts, established in 1952 to preserve and promote Indian cultural heritage.
 
• **Performing Arts:** This category includes disciplines such as classical music, folk music, dance, drama, and theatre, which are the focus of the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar.
 
• **Ustad Bismillah Khan:** A celebrated Indian shehnai player, he was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001 for his exceptional contribution to Indian music.
 
• **Other Awards by Sangeet Natak Akademi:** The Akademi also presents the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards to honor lifetime contributions to performing arts.
 
• **Eligibility for the Puraskar:** Nominees must be below 40 years of age and have demonstrated exceptional talent in their respective fields of performing arts.

questions.question: Dhanu Yatra celebration of Odisha, which is also the largest open-air theatre in the world, is based on _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishna Leela**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dhanu Yatra** is celebrated annually in Odisha and is considered the **largest open-air theatre in the world**.
 
• The festival is based on the **Krishna Leela**, depicting episodes from the life of Lord Krishna, especially his confrontation with King Kansa.
 
• The event is held in **Bargarh district**, where the entire town transforms into a stage representing Mathura and Gopapur.
 
• During the celebration, **King Kansa**
 
• Dhanu Yatra signifies the victory of good over evil, symbolizing the end of Kansa’s tyranny by Lord Krishna.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Krishna Leela:** A dramatic representation of various episodes from Lord Krishna’s life, highlighting themes of devotion, valor, and divine intervention.
 
• **King Kansa:** He is a mythological antagonist in Hindu scriptures, known for his tyranny over Mathura and attempts to kill Krishna.
 
• **Open-Air Theatre:** Dhanu Yatra is unique as it uses the entire town as a stage, allowing the audience to immerse themselves in the mythological narrative.
 
• **Duration:** The festival typically spans **11 days**, with a detailed enactment of events leading up to Kansa’s defeat.
 
• **UNESCO Recognition Efforts:** Efforts are underway to include Dhanu Yatra in UNESCO’s list of intangible cultural heritage due to its cultural significance.

questions.question: Which singer of Carnatic music was given the title of 'Bombay' by the people of Tamil Nadu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jayashri Ramnath**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Jayashri Ramnath**, popularly known as Bombay Jayashri, is a renowned Carnatic vocalist from Tamil Nadu.
 
• She earned the title 'Bombay' due to her family’s association with Mumbai (formerly Bombay) and her upbringing in the city.
 
• Jayashri is celebrated for her melodious voice, versatile music repertoire, and dedication to traditional Carnatic music.
 
• She has received numerous awards, including the prestigious **Padma Shri** in 2021 for her contributions to Indian music.
 
• Her performances have gained international acclaim, and she has represented Indian classical music on various global platforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carnatic Music**:

 
 
• Carnatic music is a classical music tradition from South India with roots in ancient Hindu practices.
 
• It emphasizes intricate compositions called kritis and improvisational techniques like raga alapana.
 
• Famous composers include Thyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, and Shyama Shastri.
 
 
 
• **Padma Awards**:
 
 
• These are the highest civilian awards in India, conferred in three categories: Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Vibhushan.
 
• They recognize achievements in art, literature, science, sports, and other fields.
 
 
 
• **International Recognition**:
 
 
• Bombay Jayashri represented Indian classical music at the Oscars with her song in the film *Life of Pi*, which was nominated for Best Original Score.
 
• She frequently collaborates with international artists, promoting Indian music globally.
 
 
 
• **Other Prominent Carnatic Singers**:
 
 
• M.S. Subbulakshmi – First musician to receive Bharat Ratna.
 
• T.M. Krishna – Known for innovative approaches to Carnatic music.
 
• Nithyasree Mahadevan – Granddaughter of the legendary D.K. Pattammal.

questions.question: Who is the cabinet minister of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry as of September 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Piyush Goyal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Piyush Goyal is the current Cabinet Minister for the Ministry of Commerce and Industry in India as of September 2024.
 
• He has held this position since May 31, 2019, under the second term of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.
 
• In addition to Commerce and Industry, Piyush Goyal has also served in portfolios like Railways, Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, and Coal.
 
• As the Commerce and Industry Minister, he has been actively involved in promoting exports, attracting foreign direct investment (FDI), and implementing key trade policies.
 
• Under his leadership, India has worked towards free trade agreements (FTAs) with multiple nations to enhance global trade relations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Commerce and Industry:**

 
 
• The Ministry of Commerce and Industry is responsible for formulating and implementing policies for India's international trade and economic growth.
 
• It consists of two departments: the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) and the Department of Commerce.
 
• Key initiatives under the ministry include 'Make in India,' 'Startup India,' and 'Ease of Doing Business' reforms.
 
 
 
• **Free Trade Agreements (FTAs):**
 
 
• FTAs are arrangements between two or more countries that aim to reduce or eliminate trade barriers like tariffs and import quotas.
 
• India has signed FTAs with countries including Japan, South Korea, and ASEAN nations.
 
• Recent negotiations under Piyush Goyal have focused on FTAs with the UK, EU, and Canada.
 
 
 
• **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI):**
 
 
• FDI involves investments made by a company or individual in one country into business interests located in another country.
 
• India has seen a significant increase in FDI inflows under Piyush Goyal's tenure, with reforms in sectors like manufacturing, retail, and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Export Promotion:**
 
 
• Export promotion refers to efforts aimed at increasing the sale of domestic goods in international markets.
 
• Under Piyush Goyal, India has introduced several export incentives and schemes like RoDTEP (Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products).
 
• Key export sectors include textiles, pharmaceuticals, IT services, and engineering goods.

questions.question: What is the meaning of geological time?

options.text: Geological events over millions of years

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Geological events over millions of years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Geological time refers to the vast time scale of Earth's history, spanning **billions of years** since the planet's formation approximately 4.6 billion years ago.
 
• It is divided into hierarchical units, such as **eons, eras, periods, epochs, and ages**, based on significant geological and biological events.
 
• These time intervals help scientists understand the **evolution of life, climate changes, and geological processes** over Earth's history.
 
• Geological time is primarily determined by studying **rock strata, fossils, and radiometric dating techniques**.
 
• Major events in Earth's history, such as the extinction of dinosaurs or the formation of continents, are marked within this framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eons:** The largest divisions of geological time, including the **Hadean, Archean, Proterozoic, and Phanerozoic eons**.
 
• **Fossil Records:** Fossils provide evidence of past life forms and help correlate the age of rock layers in different locations.
 
• **Radiometric Dating:** A method used to determine the age of rocks and fossils by measuring the decay of radioactive isotopes.
 
• **Uniformitarianism:** The principle stating that geological processes observed today have operated in the same way throughout Earth's history.
 
• **Mass Extinctions:** Events where a significant percentage of Earth's species became extinct, marking transitions between geological periods.

questions.question: The Gopatha Brahmana is related to which of the following Vedas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atharvaveda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Gopatha Brahmana** is the only Brahmana text associated exclusively with the **Atharvaveda**.
 
• It provides explanations and interpretations of the rituals and practices outlined in the Atharvaveda.
 
• The text is divided into two parts: **Pūrva (Eastern)** and **Uttara (Western)**, focusing on ritualistic aspects and philosophical discussions.
 
• Unlike other Brahmanas, the Gopatha Brahmana does not belong to a specific shakha (branch) of the Atharvaveda and is considered a general Brahmana text for the entire Veda.
 
• It is known for its unique content compared to Brahmanas of other Vedas, focusing more on theoretical knowledge than practical rituals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmanas:** Ancient Indian texts that explain the rituals, ceremonies, and sacrifices mentioned in the Vedas.
 
• **Atharvaveda:** One of the four Vedas, primarily focused on knowledge, healing, and practical wisdom.
 
• **Structure of Vedic Literature:** Consists of four parts: **Samhitas** (hymns), **Brahmanas** (rituals), **Aranyakas** (theological reflections), and **Upanishads** (philosophical teachings).
 
• **Shakhas:** Schools or branches of Vedic knowledge, each with its own traditions and interpretations.
 
• **Importance of Brahmanas:** They serve as a bridge between the hymns of the Vedas and the philosophical discussions in the Upanishads by focusing on rituals and their significance.

questions.question: Which of the following states has the LOWEST child sex ratio as per Census 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Haryana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Haryana had the **lowest child sex ratio in India** as per Census 2011, with just **834 girls per 1,000 boys**.
 
• Child sex ratio refers to the number of girls per 1,000 boys in the age group of 0-6 years, serving as a key indicator of gender disparity.
 
• The low ratio in Haryana is attributed to **gender-based discrimination**, cultural preferences for male children, and the practice of sex-selective abortions.
 
• Despite several government initiatives, Haryana continues to face challenges in addressing **deep-rooted societal biases** against girl children.
 
• States like Chhattisgarh and Arunachal Pradesh had significantly better child sex ratios, with figures such as 972 and 972 respectively, indicating **less gender disparity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Child Sex Ratio (CSR):**

 
 
• It is a demographic metric used to measure the number of girls per 1,000 boys in the age group of 0-6 years.
 
• A declining CSR is often indicative of **gender-biased practices** such as female feticide and neglect of girl children.
 
 
 
• **Reasons for Low Child Sex Ratio:**
 
 
• Societal preference for male children due to inheritance laws, economic factors, and cultural practices.
 
• Access to technology enabling **sex-selective abortions** despite legal prohibitions.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) scheme** was launched in 2015 to address the declining CSR in districts like those in Haryana.
 
• Strict implementation of the **Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act** to prevent sex-selective abortions.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Low CSR:**
 
 
• Skewed gender ratios lead to **social issues** such as increased violence against women and challenges in marriage patterns.
 
• It also reflects systemic inequality and **loss of potential human capital** due to the neglect of female children.

questions.question: According to Census of India 2001, what was the percentage of immigrant population from Afghanistan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.002**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census of India 2001, the percentage of immigrant population from Afghanistan in India was **0.002%**.
 
• The Census of India is conducted every ten years to collect demographic, social, and economic data across the country.
 
• Immigrants from Afghanistan primarily settled in regions such as Delhi, Mumbai, and other urban centers for better livelihood opportunities.
 
• Afghan immigrants in India include refugees fleeing conflict, as well as individuals seeking education, business, or family reunification.
 
• India has historically served as a host country for refugees from neighboring nations, including Afghanistan, due to its geopolitical proximity and cultural ties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census of India:**

 
 
• The Census is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• It is a comprehensive enumeration of the population, collecting data on variables such as age, gender, occupation, religion, literacy, and migration.
 
• The Census of India is one of the oldest such exercises globally, with the first census conducted in 1872.
 
• The data is used for policymaking, resource allocation, and socio-economic planning.
 
 
 
• **Immigration:**
 
 
• Immigration refers to the movement of individuals from one country to another for various reasons, including work, study, or seeking asylum.
 
• India hosts immigrants from several neighboring countries, including Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, and Sri Lanka.
 
• Immigration trends often reflect geopolitical conditions, such as wars, economic instability, or natural disasters.
 
 
 
• **Afghan Refugees:**
 
 
• India is home to many Afghan refugees who have fled political unrest, persecution, and violence in Afghanistan.
 
• India provides limited support to Afghan refugees, including access to education, healthcare, and informal employment opportunities.
 
• The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) works closely with the Indian government to assist Afghan refugees.
 
 
 
• **India-Afghanistan Relations:**
 
 
• India and Afghanistan share strong cultural, historical, and economic ties.
 
• India has been a significant development partner for Afghanistan, contributing to infrastructure, education, and healthcare projects.
 
• India's strategic proximity to Afghanistan has made it a preferred destination for Afghan immigrants over the years.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of genetic industry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Poultry farming**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Poultry farming** is an example of a genetic industry as it involves the breeding and rearing of birds, primarily chickens, for meat and eggs.
 
• Genetic industries are those that involve the cultivation, breeding, or propagation of living organisms to produce goods, such as poultry, livestock, or fisheries.
 
• In poultry farming, genetic selection is used to improve desirable traits like growth rate, egg production, and disease resistance.
 
• Unlike extractive industries (e.g., mining), genetic industries depend on renewable biological processes to sustain production over time.
 
• Poultry farming plays a critical role in agriculture by providing a sustainable source of protein and contributing to rural livelihoods worldwide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Genetic Industry**: Refers to industries involved in the cultivation or breeding of plants and animals, such as agriculture, forestry, fisheries, and animal husbandry.
 
• **Examples of Genetic Industries**: Poultry farming, dairy farming, fisheries, horticulture, and apiculture (beekeeping).
 
• **Contrast with Extractive Industries**: Extractive industries, like mining and quarrying, involve the extraction of non-renewable natural resources, while genetic industries rely on renewable resources and biological processes.
 
• **Importance of Poultry Farming**: It contributes significantly to food security, employment generation, and the economy, especially in developing countries.
 
• **Technological Advances**: Modern poultry farming uses advanced techniques such as controlled breeding, genetic engineering, and automated rearing systems to maximize production efficiency.

questions.question: When was the Dronacharya Award instituted in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1985**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Dronacharya Award was instituted in **1985** by the Government of India to honor outstanding coaches in sports and games.
 
• It is named after **Dronacharya**, the legendary mentor from the Indian epic Mahabharata, symbolizing excellence in coaching.
 
• The award recognizes coaches who have produced medal-winning athletes at international events like the Olympics, Asian Games, and Commonwealth Games.
 
• Recipients of the award receive a cash prize, a bronze statuette of Dronacharya, and a certificate of merit.
 
• The selection process is conducted annually by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award**:

 
 
• Instituted in 1991-92, it is India’s highest sporting honor, awarded for outstanding performance over a period of four years.
 
• Recipients receive a medallion, certificate, and cash prize.
 
• The award was renamed **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award** in 2021.
 
 
 
• **Arjuna Award**:
 
 
• Established in 1961, it honors athletes for consistent performance in national and international events.
 
• Recipients are awarded a bronze statuette, certificate, and cash prize.
 
 
 
• **Major Dhyan Chand Award**:
 
 
• Introduced in 2002, it is given for lifetime achievement in sports and games.
 
• Named after Major Dhyan Chand, a legendary hockey player.
 
 
 
• **National Sports Day**:
 
 
• Celebrated annually on **August 29**, marking the birth anniversary of Major Dhyan Chand.
 
• On this day, major sports awards like the Dronacharya, Arjuna, and Khel Ratna are presented.

questions.question: The ratio of 'mass by volume percentage' to 'volume by volume percentage' of a given solution gives ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**density of solute**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'mass by volume percentage' represents the **mass of the solute per 100 mL of the solution**.
 
• 'Volume by volume percentage' represents the **volume of the solute per 100 mL of the solution**.
 
• The ratio of 'mass by volume percentage' to 'volume by volume percentage' provides the **density of the solute** because density is defined as mass per unit volume.
 
• This relationship is derived from the formula: **Density = Mass / Volume**.
 
• It is important to note that this calculation assumes the volume of the solute is used directly in the denominator without considering solution interactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Density:** Density is a physical property defined as mass per unit volume, commonly expressed in units like g/mL or kg/m³.
 
• **Mass by Volume Percentage:** It is calculated as (mass of solute / volume of solution) × 100, representing the concentration of a solution.
 
• **Volume by Volume Percentage:** It is calculated as (volume of solute / volume of solution) × 100, often used for liquid-liquid solutions.
 
• **Solute and Solvent:** In a solution, the solute is the substance dissolved, while the solvent is the medium in which the solute is dissolved.
 
• **Applications:** Understanding density and concentration is crucial in fields like chemistry, biology, and material sciences for solution preparation and analysis.
